newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-FERRARI READY TO BOUNCE BACK.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FERRARI READY TO BOUNCE BACK.

text.p: Michael Schumacher left Silverstone in confident mood despite being forced to retire from Sunday's British Grand Prix with his first technical failure of the season with Ferrari.

As Canadian Jacques Villeneuve celebrated his fourth triumph of the year for Williams and the revival of his challenge, the 28-year-old German made it clear he feels confident in his ability to stay out in front in the championship.
"What happened in this race was a shame," he said. "My left rear wheel bearing failed and that was a pity because it was going to be a very good race.
"All the same, I was not too disappointed because I was comfortably in the lead when it occurred and I feel certain now that we have the race package to maintain our championship bid.
"Williams may still have a slight advantage over us in qualifying trim, but we are very competitive in the race. Anyway, technical problems happen and to the other teams as well. That is racing."

Schumacher, whose form this year has taken him and Ferrari to the top of both the drivers and the constructors' title races, had failed to finish only one previous race this year -- the Argentine Grand Prix in April when he crashed.

Since then, he has finished second once, first three times and fourth once in the five races before Britain -- a run of form that proved Ferrari's chronic reliability problems of the past had been overcome.
His team-mate Briton Eddie Irvine was also forced out of Sunday's race when he was in a strong challenging position in second place. His car suffered a broken halfshaft.
Irvine's retirement was his first technical failure of the year also. He crashed out of the Australian and Canadian races.

"This is my first mechanical problem this season and until now we have been incredibly reliable," he said. "After my experiences last year, when I seemed to be breaking down in every race, it is a total change so I although I am disappointed, I am realistic.
"My car was really good in ther ace and even though the result was not perfect, we proved we are still very competitive."
Schumacher looked a certain winner as he and Villeneuve were in a race of their own in the opening part of Sunday's 59-laps contest in front of 110,000 fans.

But misfortunes struck both of them, Villeneuve suffering a lengthy 33-second spit-stop because of a faulty left-front wheel and then Schumacher, who built up a 40-seconds lead, retiring after his second pit-stop when he was in command.

The result cut Schumacher's championship lead to just four points with eight of this year's 17 races remaining but he is favourite to reopen that advantage at his home German Grand Prix at Hockenheim on July 27.
"It will be more difficult for us in Germany," said Villeneuve. "It is not such a great track for us but I think we can fight for it everywhere we go."
The Williams' team's chief weakness as the season unfolds through the European heart of the season could turn out to be the inconsistency of Heinz-Harald Frentzen.
Villeneuve's team-mate has failed to score points in six of the nine races this year and on Sunday, after stalling on the grid, started from the pit lane and then crashed out at the first corner.
Like Schumacher, he will be in need of a boost from his home fans at Hockenheim if he is to rescue his season and help Williams retain their constructors' title.
